summary: Retested all 9 requested flows for the new-feature iteration (password reset, commission CRUD, commission-at-recharge, user edit, profile edit, dashboard quick-tiles, Google OAuth button visibility, admin-only Commissions nav, and the 422-crash retest). 13/14 backend tests pass. UI flows for forgot-password → reset → login-with-new → Settings→change-back → login-with-original all PASS. Commissions CRUD in the UI works (add role rule, add global rule, delete first, list refreshes). Admin sidebar shows Commissions; retailer sidebar has only Dashboard/Recharge/Wallet/Transactions/Settings — no Commissions and no Network. Dashboard quick-tiles preselect the correct service on /recharge (mobile_prepaid, dth, electricity, data_card). Google buttons exist with correct testids on /login and /signup. The previously-reported 422 CRA overlay crash is FIXED: submitting 'foo@bar.test' in Users → Add user now shows a readable sonner toast ('value is not a valid email address: The part after the @-sign is a special-use or reserved name…') and no overlay. HOWEVER a NEW critical backend bug is confirmed: role+service+operator commission rules are silently ignored by get_commission_rate() — a rule {role:retailer, service:mobile_prepaid, operator:airtel, rate:0.05} is never matched, so the recharge falls through to default 2%. Global service+operator rules DO work.

critical.issue: get_commission_rate() lookup list is missing the {role+service+operator} and {role+service} combos. A commission rule scoped to a role AND a specific service/operator never matches — the code falls through to the default 2%. The 6 checks all require role-scoped rules to have service=None AND operator=None, so any role-scoped rule with a service/operator filter is dead data. Verified: rule {role:retailer, service:mobile_prepaid, operator:airtel, rate:0.05} → applied rate on retailer recharge was 0.02 (default). Same rule as {role:null, service:mobile_prepaid, operator:airtel, rate:0.05} (global) → correctly applied 0.05.

minor.issue: Rules created with role='retailer' show up in the /commissions table but silently do nothing at recharge time — UX is misleading.

integration_issues.flow: Users → Edit → set new password → retailer relogin
integration_issues.issue: Playwright test could not locate the edit-{uid} button on the newly-created retailer row within 1500ms of create-submit (edit_testid returned empty string). Consequence: the Edit modal was never opened, so the password patch was not sent, and retailer login with the new password failed while the old password still worked. Backend PATCH /api/users/{id} with password is verified working via pytest (TestUserEdit.test_admin_can_edit_user_and_change_password PASSES). Suspected root cause is a UI list-refresh race after create — the row is present but paint may lag; not confirmed as a real bug. Main agent should retest manually.

issues: Recharts warning 'width(-1) height(-1)' printed to console when the volume chart container is initially 0-sized on first paint. Cosmetic — no visual impact.

action_items: HIGH: Fix get_commission_rate() in /app/backend/server.py — add rule-lookup patterns for {user_id:None, role:X, service:S, operator:O}, {user_id:None, role:X, service:S, operator:None}, and possibly {user_id:X, service:S, operator:O} already covered. Simplest fix: change the last three role checks to include service/operator variants BEFORE falling to role-only + default. e.g. append checks {user_id:None, role:user['role'], service:service, operator:operator}, {user_id:None, role:user['role'], service:service, operator:None} before the role-only match, and put role-only last.

MED: In Users.jsx EditUserModal, after PATCH success also trigger a small optimistic UI refresh (currently only onSaved()→load() which is fine, but the Playwright race suggests the DOM update lag is noticeable). Consider showing a spinner overlay on the row while updates propagate.
LOW: The commission-rules table doesn't reveal which rule will actually apply; add a tooltip or badge indicating role-scoped rules with service/operator are 'preview only' until backend fix lands.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_commission_rate is a hidden matcher — no test covered the role+service+operator combo. Add unit test in backend when fixing.

server.py — /auth/session accepts an invalid session_id and returns 400, but the code also does a synchronous `requests.get` inside an async endpoint (blocks event loop). Consider httpx.AsyncClient for the Emergent session exchange.
server.py forgot-password always returns the reset_token in the response body. Fine for demo but should be gated by an env flag (e.g. DEMO_MODE=true) to prevent token disclosure in production.
Users.jsx EditUserModal always sends `status: f.status` in the body even when unchanged; harmless because PATCH is additive, but a diff-based body would be cleaner and cheaper.
Recharge.jsx line 23 still calls `r.data[service][0].code` without optional chaining on `r.data[service]` — will throw if a future service code is added to SERVICES but missing in the OPERATORS map.

success_rate.frontend: 8/9 flows PASS; 1 UI-timing flake on user-edit-password

rca of the issue: Root cause of the failed commission-at-recharge test: /app/backend/server.py::get_commission_rate defines only 6 candidate query patterns; none of them ever match a document whose fields are {user_id:None, role:'retailer', service:'mobile_prepaid', operator:'airtel'}. Reproduction: (1) Admin creates rule role=retailer/service=mobile_prepaid/operator=airtel/rate=0.05, (2) retailer with wallet ≥100 recharges mobile_prepaid+airtel ₹100, (3) resulting tx.commission_rate is 0.02 (default) or the value of whatever role-only rule exists, NOT 0.05. Mitigation: extend the `checks` list in get_commission_rate() to include role+service+operator and role+service combos before the role-only fallback. Suggested patch: `checks = [ {user_id: uid, service: s, operator: o}, {user_id: uid, service: s, operator: None}, {user_id: uid, service: None, operator: None}, {user_id: None, role: None, service: s, operator: o}, {user_id: None, role: None, service: s, operator: None}, {user_id: None, role: r, service: s, operator: o}, {user_id: None, role: r, service: s, operator: None}, {user_id: None, role: r, service: None, operator: None} ]`.
